tasks.spec:
You are a READ-ONLY diagnostic scout with a MEASUREMENT budget for the OBE podcast repo at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast. You may read any file in that repo and you MUST run real ffmpeg/ffprobe renders, but you MUST NOT modify, create, or delete anything inside that repo: no source/test/config edits, no git commit/checkout/stash, no running the orchestrator or the driver scripts, no writing into episodes/. `git -C /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast status --porcelain` must be identical at the end of your run to what it was at the start -- capture both into probe.log. Your ONLY writable location is your current scratch task directory (probe.json, probe.log, report.md, and any temp renders you put in a subdir of it). No network. No publish/send/social/CRM/S3/deploy. Do NOT call any LLM/model from the pipeline and do NOT load skills or MCP tools. Subscription/OAuth engines only, zero API spend. Use PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp for every python invocation.

MISSION CONTEXT: episode 2026-06-10-fred-cho is the end-to-end proof run for a 100%-hands-off podcast pipeline. Twelve prior rounds fixed the media/render gates. The current and ONLY blocker is this, from the 2026-07-24 13:21 shadow run (render.log):
  angle_render: program AUDIO disagrees with the map (audio=2.453000 map_total=2.500000) - sample-exact trims should make these equal; refusing the render (fail-closed)
which surfaced to the orchestrator as media_gate angle_segments: 'angle segment 23 did not render' (measurements.segment_index=23), stage=error, no final/episode.mp4.

EXACT MECHANISM YOU ARE DIAGNOSING (verify every line number yourself, they are from HEAD on branch fix/single-pass-program-audio):
1. server/pipeline/orchestrator.py lines ~2637-2670, function _gated_angle_renderer: the angle_segments GATE renders EVERY planned segment INDIVIDUALLY by calling the real renderer with a ONE-ELEMENT segment list and crossfade_s=0.0: original_angle_renderer([segment], host_path, guest_path, composite_path, render_offsets, segment_path, crossfade_s=0.0). A None/missing return becomes 'angle segment N did not render'. So the failing unit is a SINGLE-SEGMENT (n==1) render, roughly 2.5 seconds long, NOT the full program.
2. server/pipeline/angle_render.py render_angle_switch(): each piece is rendered video-only, ffprobe'd for frame count (_piece_frame_duration, ~line 122), the boundary map total is sum(nb_frames)/30 (_build_boundary_map_from_durations, ~line 646), and the program audio is built in one sample-exact atrim pass (_build_program_audio_filter, ~line 667-739) whose span for n==1 is start_sample=round(start*48000), end_sample=start_sample+round(actual_duration*48000).
3. The audio is muxed with -c:a aac (~lines 906-915), then the whole thing is re-encoded by cfr_timeline_clean_cmd (server/pipeline/video_assembly.py ~lines 469-501) which encodes audio to AAC A SECOND TIME.
4. The self-check that failed is angle_render.py ~lines 941-960: audio_duration = _stream_duration(out_path, 'a:0') (~line 103: ffprobe -show_entries stream=duration, i.e. the CONTAINER's stream duration field) and it returns None (fails the render) when abs(audio_duration - map_total) * 30 > 1.0.

THE DECISIVE QUESTION: is the program audio GENUINELY 47ms short of the map (a real render defect that would desync a viewer), or does the container's 'duration' field merely READ short (AAC encoder delay / priming / edit-list accounting across two AAC encodes) while the DECODED SAMPLE COUNT is exactly right? Answer it with measurements, not reasoning.

EXPERIMENT (this is the work; run it, do not simulate it):
Build a small harness IN YOUR SCRATCH DIR (e.g. probe_seg.py) that imports the repo (sys.path.insert of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast) and calls server.pipeline.angle_render.render_angle_switch DIRECTLY on the real composite at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/composite.mp4 (composite video stream 2842.200s / 85267 frames at 30fps, audio stream 2919.601s at 48kHz; the on-air content window is 411s-2570s, so pick starts well inside it, e.g. 700s). Pass host_video=guest_video=composite, offsets={} (or whatever the signature requires -- read it), crossfade_s=0.0, out_path inside your scratch dir, and target_size=(640,360) -- the module's own docstring states the frame-count timeline arithmetic is resolution-independent, so the small size proves the same thing in a fraction of the time. NEVER write an output next to the episode.
Run AT MINIMUM these single-segment (n==1, exactly the gate's shape) experiments and record every number:
  a) requested_duration_s = 2.5 (the failing case)
  b) requested_duration_s = 5.0
  c) requested_duration_s >= 60.0 (use 120.0 if time allows) -- THIS is what separates a FIXED per-render offset from an ACCUMULATING drift. A fixed ~47ms offset that is identical at 2.5s and at 120s is an encoder-delay artifact; a delta that grows with length is real drift.
Strongly preferred additionally: one MULTI-segment render (n=3, contiguous or with a small gap) to show whether the n>1 path behaves the same.
For EVERY experiment measure and record:
  - final_video_frames: ffprobe packet or frame count of the FINAL out_path video stream
  - map_total_s: the boundary map total the render produced (read the .boundaries.json sidecar written next to out_path, or the last edited_end_s it computed)
  - container_audio_duration_s: EXACTLY what the failing check reads -- ffprobe -v quiet -select_streams a:0 -show_entries stream=duration -of default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1 <final>
  - decoded_audio_samples: the TRUE decoded sample count -- ffprobe -count_samples -select_streams a:0 -show_entries stream=nb_read_samples (this literal token must appear in probe.log)
  - decoded_audio_duration_s: decoded_audio_samples / 48000
  - the same container-vs-decoded pair for the INTERMEDIATE program_muxed.mp4 if you can capture it (set a temp dir you control or re-run the two ffmpeg commands yourself from the module's own command construction) so you can attribute the loss to the mux encode, the cfr clean encode, or both
Capture every command you run and its raw output into probe.log.

DELIVERABLES (all three, in your scratch dir):
1. probe.json -- {"experiments": [ {"label":..., "source_start_s":..., "requested_duration_s":..., "final_video_frames":..., "map_total_s":..., "container_audio_duration_s":..., "decoded_audio_samples":..., "decoded_audio_duration_s":...}, ... ], "verdict": "<one sentence: container-duration measurement artifact, or genuine audio shortfall, and why>"}. decoded_audio_duration_s MUST equal decoded_audio_samples/48000 (the receipt checks this).
2. probe.log -- raw commands + raw ffprobe/ffmpeg output, plus the before/after `git status --porcelain` of the podcast repo.
3. report.md with these EXACT headings:
'## What was measured' (the table of experiments, with the fixed-vs-accumulating conclusion stated in milliseconds and samples)
'## Root cause' (where the 47ms goes: mux AAC encode, cfr clean AAC encode, edit list, atrim arithmetic -- with file:line citations into angle_render.py and video_assembly.py)
'## Is the check or the render wrong' (a plain verdict: the self-check at angle_render.py ~941-960 measures the wrong quantity, OR the render really is short; give the evidence for the verdict and the evidence AGAINST the other option)
'## Fix design' (the smallest change, with exact file, function, and the replacement comparison spelled out. If the fix is to compare DECODED SAMPLES instead of the container duration field, give the exact ffprobe invocation and the exact integer-sample tolerance and justify that tolerance in samples. If the fix is a tolerance widening, you must prove in numbers that the new tolerance still fails the historical defects.)
'## Proof command' (the EXACT pytest command a fix worker must run -- name the test file under /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/tests/ and the assertions the new test must make)
'## Risks' (what could make this fix mask a real desync)

HARD CONSTRAINT ON THE FIX DESIGN: this self-check exists because sub-threshold per-segment error accumulated to a measured -366ms by mid-episode on this very episode (2026-07-23) and because an earlier -shortest bug silently dropped 40 video frames. Your fix MUST still catch both of those. A fix that simply widens the tolerance until the failure disappears, or that skips the check for short programs without proving the quantity being compared was wrong, is FORBIDDEN and you must say so explicitly if you are tempted by it. Deny-by-default stands: when the audio genuinely cannot be certified against the map, the render must still fail closed.
tasks.verified: The worker actually rendered short AND long single-segment angle programs off Fred's real composite and probed each one's container audio duration against its decoded 48kHz sample count and its frame-count map total, with self-consistent numbers (decoded_audio_samples/48000 == decoded_audio_duration_s) and raw nb_read_samples evidence in probe.log -- proving whether the 47ms shortfall is a container-duration measurement artifact or a genuine audio deficit, and delivering a fail-closed fix design that still catches the historical -366ms accumulation and 40-frame drop
